That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call for the entire record pertaining to the land acquisition proceeding initiated by the Land Acquisition Officer concerning the land of petitioner being khasra No. 290/10 situated at village Parsulidih, Patwari Halka No. 23, Raipur,
Tahsil and District Raipur for its kind perusal.

10.2 That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue an appropriate writ directing the respondent authorities to conclude the land acquisition proceeding expeditiously strictly in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 within an out time limit of 3 months and after determining the compensation payable, make payment of the same in accordance with law.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 10.4 Any other relief, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper, in the facts and circumstances of the case."

2. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner is owner of the land bearing khasra no.
290/10 situated at village Parsulidih, Tahsil and District Raipur.

Respondents No. 4 to 6 have constructed public road on the aforementioned land owned by petitioner without initiating any proceeding of land acquisition or making payment of suitable amount of compensation of the land of petitioner.
Petitioner thereafter made several representations along with demarcation report of the concerned revenue officials to Respondent No. 3/ Land Acquisition Officer-cum-Sub-Divisional Officer(R.).
Based on the representation supported with demarcation report, Respondent No. 3 issued letter to Respondent No. 6 for taking steps for land acquisition.

Accordingly, Respondent No.
6 sent letter to Respondent No. 2/ Collector, requesting for initiating land acquisition proceeding of the land owned by petitioner measuring 1.170 Hectare.
Letter to Collector is dated 26.05.2023 (Annexure P-7).

Respondent No. 2 based on the request made by Respondent No. 6 has issued a notification under Section 11 of t he Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "Act of 2013").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The notification was issued on 13.09.2023 and it was published on 15.09.2023 in the Gazette, however, Respondents No. 4 to 6 have not deposited the amount of compensation till date, as calculated by Respondent No.
3, even after lapse of about 4 months and therefore direction be issued to Respondents No. 4 to 6 to comply with the letter issued by Respondent No. 3 on 23.04.2024 and to deposit the amount of compensation calculated at the earliest.
3.

Learned State counsel submits that in view of the submission of learned counsel for petitioner based on the documents that land acquisition proceedings have already been initiated for acquisition of land as mentioned in the Gazette notification dated 15.09.2023 and the letter sent by Respondent No. 3 to Respondent No. 6, she is having no objection to the limited prayer made by counsel for petitioner.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents placed on record.

sentences.text: 5. Perusal of documents would show that Respondent No. 6 has requested to Respondent No. 2 to initiate proceeding for land acquisition, accordingly the District Collector-cum-ex-officio Secretary to the State Government has issued notification under Section 11 (1) of the Act of 2013 for acquiring the land measuring 1.170 Hect. is of Khasra no. 290/10 which is reflecting from the letter written by Respondent No. 6 to Respondent No. 2 which is stated to be the land owned by petitioner.

Respondent No. 3 has further issued letter to Respondent No. 6 computing the amount of compensation to be deposited for concluding the land acquisition proceedings initiated pursuant to Gazette notification dated 15.09.2023.

Respondents No. 4 to 6 have not deposited the said amount,
as stated by learned counsel for petitioner.

6. In the aforementioned facts of the case, instead of keeping this writ petition pending, it will be in the interest of justice to dispose of this writ petition directing Respondents No. 4 to 6 to comply with the letter dated 23.04.2024, Annexure P-10, written by Respondent No. 3, expeditiously.

Accordingly, the respondents No. 4 to 6 are directed to take all necessary steps for complying with the letter dated 23.04.2024 of Land Acquisition Officer expeditiously, preferably within a further period of 03 months from the date of receipt of order passed by this Court.
7. With the aforesaid observations and direction, this writ petition stands disposed of.

Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) Judge pwn Mohammad Asgar vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 September, 2024
